Fastbloom Terms of Use

Effective October 13, 2026 · Last updated October 13, 2026

In plain English: your use of Fastbloom is governed by Apple's standard app license, plus the extra terms below. Fastbloom is a tracking and education tool, not a medical device or medical advice; check with a doctor before fasting if you have a health condition. Subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel, and a free trial turns into a paid subscription unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends.

If you are struggling with eating or are in crisis, call your local emergency number. In the US or Canada, call or text 988. Elsewhere, see findahelpline.com. Eating-disorder helplines: Fastbloom Support.

Apple's Standard EULA

Fastbloom is licensed to you, not sold, under Apple's Licensed Application End User License Agreement (the "Standard EULA"). The Standard EULA, including its sections on the scope of the license, consent to use of data, termination, warranty disclaimers, limitation of liability, export rules and governing law, applies to Fastbloom. These Terms of Use add app-specific terms. If these terms and the Standard EULA conflict, the Standard EULA controls, except where these terms give you more rights. We (the developer of Fastbloom), not Apple, are responsible for Fastbloom and its support. Apple is a third-party beneficiary of the Standard EULA and may enforce it.

By downloading or using Fastbloom you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the app. Our Privacy Policy explains how data is handled.

Not medical advice

  • Fastbloom is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. Fasting plans, timers, stage descriptions, articles in Learn and recaps are general information for healthy adults, not medical advice.
  • Health information in the app cites its sources and labels how strong the evidence is. Research on fasting is still developing and may not apply to you.
  • GLP-1 and side-effect logs are a personal record only. Fastbloom does not recommend doses, timing or changes to any medication. Follow your prescriber's instructions.
  • Talk to a doctor before you start fasting if you have diabetes or take blood-sugar-lowering medication, have a heart, kidney or other medical condition, take prescription medicines, are pregnant or breastfeeding, are underweight, or have ever had an eating disorder. Stop fasting and get medical help if you feel faint, confused, very weak or unwell.
  • Fastbloom is not a crisis or emergency service and nobody monitors what you enter. The eating-disorder and crisis helplines listed in the app are independent services; we are not affiliated with them and are not responsible for their services.

Fasting safety and age limits

Fastbloom is meant for adults. The optional safety check during onboarding asks whether you are under 18, pregnant or breastfeeding, have a history of an eating disorder, or take diabetes medication. Fasts of 24 hours or longer are offered only to adults who report none of these, with extra safety guidance. These limits rely on what you tell the app and are not a substitute for medical advice. You are responsible for deciding whether fasting is right for you.

Weekly recap and AI-generated text

Where your iPhone supports it, the weekly recap is written automatically by Apple's on-device Foundation Models; otherwise it uses a built-in template. Nobody reviews recaps, and AI-written text can be incomplete or wrong. Recaps describe your own logs; they are not medical advice. Apple controls the on-device model, and we can't promise it will be available on every device or behave the same over time.

Using Fastbloom

Fastbloom is not directed at children. If you are under the age of majority where you live, use it only with the permission of a parent or guardian, who also agrees to these terms for purchases; extended fasts are not available to people under 18. Features may differ between versions and devices and may change as we improve the app.

Free version and ads

Fasting with the timer and the eating-disorder and crisis resources are free; other features described in the app, such as history beyond the free window and the weekly recap, need Fastbloom Pro. The free version shows ads served by third-party ad networks through AppLovin MAX: banners only on the History and Learn lists, plus at most one full-screen ad per session after you log a fast, starting from your third fast. Helplines are never shown next to ads. We are not responsible for the content of third-party ads or the websites or apps they link to. Rewarded ads may unlock a small bonus described in the app (one weekly recap, or 7 extra days of history); rewards have no cash value, cannot be transferred and may change.

Fastbloom Pro: subscriptions, free trial and lifetime purchase

The free version of Fastbloom includes ads and the features described in the app as free. Fastbloom Pro unlocks the Pro features and removes ads. Pro is available as:

  • An auto-renewing subscription (yearly, and any other period offered in the app). The yearly plan may include a 7-day free trial for eligible new subscribers, as an Apple introductory offer.
  • A lifetime purchase: a one-time, non-consumable purchase. No renewals.

The price, billing period and trial length are shown in the app before you confirm and in Apple's purchase sheet. Prices vary by country and may include taxes.

How billing works

  • Payment is charged to your Apple ID account when you confirm the purchase. If you start a free trial, you are not charged during the trial; your Apple ID is charged the subscription price when the trial ends unless you cancel at least 24 hours before it ends.
  • Subscriptions renew automatically unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Your account is charged for renewal within the 24 hours before the current period ends, at the then-current price.
  • You can manage or cancel a subscription at any time in iOS Settings > [your name] > Subscriptions, or from the "Manage subscription" option in the app's Settings. Cancelling stops future renewals; you keep Pro until the end of the period you paid for. If you cancel during a free trial, Apple may end your access to Pro right away.
  • Any unused part of a free trial is forfeited when you buy a subscription or the lifetime purchase.
  • If a price increases, Apple notifies you in advance and, where required, asks for your consent before renewing at the new price.
  • If you have a subscription and later buy the lifetime purchase, cancel the subscription in Settings so you are not charged twice. The app reminds you.
  • Purchases are shareable with up to five other family members through Apple's Family Sharing, where the app says so.

Refunds and restores

All payments are processed by Apple. We cannot see or issue refunds; request one from Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com. Apple's refund decisions and your statutory rights (for example, EU/UK withdrawal rights for digital content) are handled by Apple under its terms. Use "Restore Purchases" in the app to get Pro back on a new device signed in to the same Apple ID.

For Fastbloom, Pro is offered as Fastbloom Pro Yearly (US$24.99 per year in the US), with a 7-day free trial for eligible new subscribers, and Fastbloom Pro Lifetime (US$44.99 in the US), a one-time purchase. The current price in your currency is shown in the app and in Apple's purchase sheet before you confirm.

Your data

What you log in Fastbloom stays on your device; only a small copy of your fasts (start and end times, goal and plan name) is kept in your own iCloud, which you can switch off in the app. You are responsible for keeping your device, Apple ID and anything you share secure, and for keeping backups. We cannot recover data you delete or lose because we never have a copy.

Acceptable use

Don't use Fastbloom to break the law or anyone else's rights; don't use buddy codes or shared images to harass anyone or to promote harmful eating; don't try to reverse-engineer, tamper with or bypass the app's purchase checks, safety limits or ad systems, except where the law allows this despite this restriction; and don't use automated means to generate fake ad impressions or rewards.

Disclaimers and liability

Fastbloom is provided "as is" and "as available", as described in the Standard EULA. We work to keep the app's information accurate and its sources current, but we do not guarantee that the app, its articles, timers, recaps or calculations are free of errors. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for health decisions you make based on the app, for missed notifications or reminders, or for the loss of data stored on your device, and our total liability is limited as described in the Standard EULA. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law, or rights you have under consumer law in your country that cannot be waived.

Changes

We may update these terms, for example when we add features. We will change the date at the top and, for significant changes, tell you in the app. Continuing to use Fastbloom after a change means you accept the updated terms. Changes never apply retroactively to purchases you already made.
